rows: A recruitment channel for central government departments, Income Tax, Central Excise/GST, Customs, CBI, Ministry of External Affairs, Audit and Accounts, and dozens of others, through SSC CGL (graduate-level, Group B/C posts) and SSC CHSL (12th-pass-level, Group C posts like LDC/JSA and DEO).

A recruitment channel for public sector bank officer and clerk posts through IBPS (common exam for 11 public sector banks) and SBI's own separate PO and Clerk exams. You end up working inside one specific bank, not a general government cadre.
One conducting body (SSC) with two main exams (CGL and CHSL) plus a few specialised ones (CPO, JE, Stenographer). One notification cycle a year for CGL.

Two separate systems: IBPS PO/Clerk (covers 11 banks in one exam) and SBI PO/Clerk (SBI runs its own separate exam). Many aspirants sit both, plus RRB and regional rural bank exams, in the same prep cycle.

Postings spread across dozens of departments and cities depending on the post you get; some roles (Customs, IB) mean port cities or metros, others (Inspector of Income Tax) mean district or state postings.
Postings are branch-based within one bank's network, which can include rural and semi-urban branches, especially in your first few years, this is a structural part of the role, not an exception.

figures.label: Education Budget
figures.source: Both tracks typically need 4-8 months of serious, structured prep for a first realistic attempt, and most successful candidates do not clear on their first try, plan for 1-2 attempt cycles, not one shot. Bank exams run more frequent cycles across IBPS and SBI in the same year, which means more attempts per year if you fail one round. SSC CGL usually runs one main notification cycle a year, so a missed or failed attempt costs you a full year, not a few months.

figures.label: Pay Range
figures.source: If your family or financial runway cannot absorb 1-2 years of exam-focused prep without income, that constraint should weigh as heavily as which exam "suits your brain" better. Building a parallel, high-income skill, something you can freelance or monetise while you prepare, protects that runway and moves you toward financial freedom even before results are out.
